title: Sales Enablement Playbook — Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pitch Decks, Pricing Guidance, Case Studies & Security FAQ
author: Ava Thompson
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook provides unified sales enablement artifacts and guidance for field reps and pre-sales engineers to articulate Redwood Inference's value, handle competitive conversations, structure pitch decks, present pricing and packaging, and answer common security questions from prospects. Use this as the canonical source for presentations, battlecards, and customer-facing takeaways.

Audience: Sales, Solutions Engineering, Customer Success, and GTM marketing.

Primary outcomes:
- Faster deal cycles through consistent positioning and objections handling.
- Reduced risk in technical diligence via a standard security FAQ and reference assets.
- Clear pricing guardrails and examples to accelerate quote generation.

Ownership and lifecycle
- Playbook owner: go-to-market (Ava Thompson)
- Content owners: Product (positioning and roadmap), Eng-Serving-Runtime (performance claims), Security (security FAQ and evidence), Finance (pricing guidance)
- Review cadence: quarterly or on major product/pricing updates

1) Positioning & Messaging

Core positioning (1-liner): Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that makes high-performance, reliable LLM serving predictable and economical across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Key pillars (talking points):
- Production-first: SLA-backed Dedicated and robust private deployment options with tracing, rollouts, and observability.
- Cost-aware performance: Batching, prefix/KV caching, and quantization profiles that reduce per-token cost while preserving quality.
- Unified API: Same REST/SDK interface and rollout semantics across hosted, dedicated and private deployments — reduces integration and ops work.
- Reliability & graceful degradation: Smart routing, multi-variant fallbacks, and auto-fallback policies keep applications online under capacity pressure.

Elevator pitch (30s):
"Redwood Inference gives engineering teams a single place to run low-latency, cost-effective LLM inference — whether you want the fastest hosted API, reserved Dedicated capacity, or a VPC/on-prem private deployment. We combine a GPU-optimized runtime, automated caching and batching, and enterprise controls so you can ship LLM features with predictable latency, lower unit cost, and enterprise-grade security."

Message tailoring by persona:
- Engineering/ML Lead: Emphasize runtime kernel selection, batching, quantization profiles, and per-route tracing. Provide perf benchmarks and SDK examples.
- Platform/Infra: Emphasize Dedicated capacity, autoscaling policies, network isolation, and Terraform modules.
- Product/PM: Emphasize cost predictability, quality monitoring and regression alerts, and rollout controls.
- Security/Compliance: Emphasize audit logging, KMS/HSM integration, private control plane, and SOC/ISO artifacts availability.

Common objections & responses (short):
- "We can self-host cheaper": Response — total cost includes engineering ops, model updates, and reliability. Redwood reduces time-to-production and provides cost optimization levers tied to measurable unit economics.
- "We already use X cloud provider service": Response — Redwood provides consistent runtime behavior across hosted, dedicated, and private options, with observability and fallbacks that are tuned for inference workloads.

2) Competitive Briefs

High-level competitive landscape: cloud-hosted model endpoints, LLM API providers, and inference infrastructure vendors.

Competitive matrix (summary):
- Redwood vs managed cloud endpoints: Redwood focuses on inference-optimized runtime, cost controls (batching/caching), and hybrid deployment modes (private + dedicated).
- Redwood vs API-first LLM providers: Redwood emphasizes production-grade SLAs, rollout controls, and observability for large-scale deployments.
- Redwood vs self-hosted runtimes: Redwood provides a unified control plane and optional private deployments to reduce ops burden while preserving isolation.

Sample battlecard (short):
- Competitor: CloudX Model Endpoints
  - Strengths: deep cloud integration, broad model catalog
  - Weaknesses: higher per-token cost at scale, limited fallback/rollout primitives, less inference optimizations for latency-sensitive workloads
  - Redwood talking points: predictable Dedicated capacity, kernel-level optimizations, and intelligent batching that reduce unit costs while improving tail latency

- Competitor: OpenServe Runtime
  - Strengths: flexible self-hosted control
  - Weaknesses: operational burden, lack of standardized observability and SLA offering
  - Redwood talking points: same developer API across environments, optional private control plane with Redwood-managed observability and enterprise support

3) Pitch Deck Guidance and Slide Architecture

Recommended deck length: 10–14 slides for a first technical-sales presentation. Prioritize: problem, customer impact, Redwood solution, demo outline, pricing, case studies, security/compliance, next steps.

Core slide-by-slide outline:
1. Title + Value Prop (30s)
2. The Problem (customer's pain: latency, cost, ops)
3. Why Existing Options Fall Short (3 bullets)
4. Redwood Solution Overview (hosted, dedicated, private)
5. How It Works (runtime, smart routing, caching, batching)
6. Performance & Cost Benchmarks (3 example workloads)
7. Deployment Models & SLAs (hosted, dedicated, private)
8. Security & Compliance (auditability, KMS, private control plane)
9. Pricing & Packaging (examples and a sample quote)
10. Case Studies (2 short customer stories)
11. Roadmap (relevant near-term features)
12. Demo / Technical Deep Dive (if requested)
13. Next Steps / POC Proposal

Demo checklist for SEs:
- Show REST/SDK quickstart and streaming response flow
- Demonstrate model rollout and canary rules in Console
- Run a short perf test (30s) to show latency under a realistic prompt distribution
- Pull a token-level cost breakdown in Console

4) Pricing Guidance (field reference)

Principles: pricing should be transparent, predictable, and align incentives for efficient inference. Use tiered elements: hosted usage, embeddings pricing, Dedicated committed capacity, and enterprise add-ons.

Pricing components (example guardrails):
- Hosted API: per-token generation pricing tiers (standard, high-throughput). Provide example monthly spend ranges for small (<$1k), medium ($1k–$20k), large (>$20k) customers based on typical prompt lengths.
- Embeddings: per-embedding unit price with volume discounts.
- Dedicated: Monthly committed capacity (GPU-hour equivalent) with baseline throughput and optional burst capacity.
- Private deployment: Platform fee + optional support and compliance add-ons.

Sample pricing scenarios (illustrative):
- Early-stage startup POC: Hosted API + limited embeddings; expected spend $500–$2k/month.
- Growing product team: Mixed Hosted + Dedicated reserved pool for peak traffic; expected committed spend $10k–$50k/month.
- Enterprise regulated workload: Private deployment with platform fee + dedicated support; multi-year commitment recommended.

Guidance for discounting and approvals:
- Up to 10% discount: L1 AE approval
- 10–25%: Sales Director + Finance approval
- >25%: VP Sales + Finance + RevOps approval

Quote checklist before submission:
1. Confirm deployment model and baseline throughput requirements
2. Validate expected token volumes and embedding units
3. Identify compliance add-ons and data residency needs
4. Confirm length of commitment and SLA requirements

5) Case Studies (battle-tested, short narratives)

Structure for each case study: Customer background, challenge, solution (how Redwood was used), measurable outcomes (latency, cost, reliability), and contactable reference. Keep stories concise and metric-driven.

Example case study A:
- Customer: FinTech platform (mid-market)
- Challenge: Latency spikes and high inference cost on customer-facing chatbot under peak loads
- Solution: Moved inference to Redwood Dedicated with autoscaling policies, enabled KV caching for prefixes, and applied quantization profiles for lower-cost variants for non-critical routes
- Outcomes: 2.5x reduction in 99th percentile latency, 40% reduction in per-token operational cost, improved uptime during Black Friday-style traffic

Example case study B:
- Customer: Health SaaS (regulated)
- Challenge: Need for private deployment and strict audit trails for PHI-handling inference
- Solution: Private deployment with customer-managed network, KMS integration, and retention policies configured per contract
- Outcomes: Successful external audit, zero data-exfiltration incidents, and 98.9% inference uptime SLA met in first 12 months

6) Security FAQ for Prospects (Top-level answers + where to find evidence)

Q: How do you isolate customer data in Dedicated and Private deployments?
A: Dedicated runs in isolated GPU pools with tenant-level isolation, network segmentation, and per-tenant storage. Private offers a customer-managed VPC/on-prem option with an optional private control plane. We share architecture diagrams and network boundary configs on request.

Q: Do you support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM)?
A: Yes. For Private and Dedicated customers we support customer-managed KMS integrations; HSM options available for high-security contracts.

Q: What logs and audit trails do you provide?
A: Token-level cost/latency breakdowns, per-request trace IDs, request/response metadata (content redaction options), and admin audit logs for configuration changes. Retention windows configurable per contract.

Q: How is PHI and PII handled?
A: We provide deployment patterns and contractual controls for regulated workloads: private deployment, encrypted-at-rest keys, strict retention policies, and SOC/ISO compliance artifacts where applicable. We recommend an architecture review with Security engineering for PHI workloads.

Q: How are vulnerabilities and incident response handled?
A: We maintain an incident response process with customer notification SLAs, monthly security patching for managed components, and a public CVE handling policy. Customers can opt into additional SLA-backed incident response services.

Q: Can we get pen test and compliance evidence?
A: Yes. We provide SOC/ISO summaries and selected pen test reports under NDA. For enterprise deals, coordinate with the Security team (security@redwood.ai) to set up evidence sharing.

Security artifacts and where to get them:
